Synopsis:
In these dialogues, Zevlor reflects on what's happened (an attack of goblins at the gate, which the player helped with) and his mistrust of and bitterness towards the druids who are reluctantly hosting his people. He is exasperated, furious, but also eager to meet anyone who could help. He'll show a flash of anger and frustration at the start if the player struck him, but is pragmatic enough to calm himself once he realises you could be more help to him than harm.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_TieflingLeader_DenIntro.json: This takes place just after a goblin attack at the grove gate that the player helped repel. Zevlor speaks for a band of tiefling refugees from Elturel (shocked by the city’s “Descent”) and is bitter and mistrustful of the druids who have been reluctantly hosting them. He initially flashes anger (especially if provoked or struck), then composes himself when he realises the player saved the grove and could actually help. Off‑screen, the druids — led by the new First Druid Kagha — are beginning a ritual to cut the grove off and are forcing outsiders out, so Zevlor hopes the player might persuade Kagha to buy his people more time.
- DEN_TieflingLeader.json: In these dialogues, Zevlor reflects on what's happened (an attack of goblins at the gate, which the player helped with) and his mistrust of and bitterness towards the druids who are reluctantly hosting his people. He is exasperated, furious, but also eager to meet anyone who could help. In the same dialogue, we can also uncover that he is in fact a traitor, concerned only with getting these people through the goblins so he can trade them for his own safety later. In truth he is resentful and contemptuous of them, viewing them as weak.
- DEN_AttackOnDen_TieflingLeader.json: Zevlor is tense - he's awaiting a long-expected attack on the grove, and the player is likely here to confirm it or perhaps even strike the first blow against him. Zevlor's usual tone is all stiff upper-lip, but at certain points we'll see the cracks start to form.
- DEN_AdventurerLeader.json: Adventurer leader dialogue. Mostly used during Adventurers Quest. This is after the player has stopped Zevlor and Aradin from fighting one another. Aradin returns to his den to lick his wounds.
- DEN_TieflingLeader_AD_DenIntro.json: Zevlor is looking over the Grove after the Raiding Party Confrontation (or looking at Aradin if Aradin is KO)

Zevlor speaks for a band of tiefling refugees from Elturel (shocked by the city’s “Descent”) and is bitter and mistrustful of the druids who have been reluctantly hosting them. He initially flashes anger (especially if provoked or struck), then composes himself when he realises the player saved the grove and could actually help. Off‑screen, the druids — led by the new First Druid Kagha — are beginning a ritual to cut the grove off and are forcing outsiders out, so Zevlor hopes the player might persuade Kagha to buy his people more time.

In these dialogues, Zevlor reflects on what's happened (an attack of goblins at the gate, which the player helped with) and his mistrust of and bitterness towards the druids who are reluctantly hosting his people. He is exasperated, furious, but also eager to meet anyone who could help. In the same dialogue, we can also uncover that he is in fact a traitor, concerned only with getting these people through the goblins so he can trade them for his own safety later. In truth he is resentful and contemptuous of them, viewing them as weak.

Zevlor is tense - he's awaiting a long-expected attack on the grove, and the player is likely here to confirm it or perhaps even strike the first blow against him. Zevlor's usual tone is all stiff upper-lip, but at certain points we'll see the cracks start to form.

context: Just after a goblin attack at the grove gate — an attack the player helped repel — Zevlor speaks for a band of tiefling refugees from Elturel who have taken shelter in the druids' grove. He is bitter and mistrustful of the druids (and of outsiders in general), still smarting from how his people were treated after the Descent. Off‑screen the druids, led by the new First Druid Kagha, have begun a ritual to cut the grove off and are forcing outsiders out, so Zevlor is desperate: his people can't stay, but they risk slaughter if they leave. He may flash anger (especially if provoked or struck) and justifiably regretted an earlier outburst at Aradin, but he calms when he realises the player saved the grove and sees you as someone who might persuade Kagha to buy his people more time.
